newsitem.title: UK: Tesco nudges higher after in-line results.
newsitem.headline: Tesco nudges higher after in-line results.

text.p: Shares in Tesco Plc were marked slightly higher in early trading on Tuesday while rivals dropped as Tesco's results showed sales continuing to grow after a series of marketing initiatives.
However analysts said Tesco's results were in line with expectations with little initially to excite the stock.

"It's very much steady as she goes," said one. "Given that we had a briefing before the year end the market had a pretty good feel for how things were going. The big hit on margins was due to the petrol price war but we've known about that for some time."
Tesco shares were up 2p at 354-1/2 by 0712 GMT, while Sainsbury Plc was down 2-1/2p at 330-1/2 and Safeway Plc was down 1/2p at 364.

The supermarket group said pre-tax profit rose 10.1 percent to 750 million stg, in line with analyst expectations which ranged from 681 million stg to 760 million, according to the Estimate Directory.
The dividend was raised 7.8 percent to 10.35p, also in line with expectations.
UK same-store sales rose 7.5 percent though the petrol price war cut UK profit growth by some five percent and lowered overall operating margins by about 0.3 percent.

Tesco said sales had continued to move ahead in the early weeks of the current year, with same store sales up 6.0 percent from the year before, though price inflation had dropped to 1.0 percent from 3.5 percent in the second half of last year.
The company, which higlighted recent successful marketing initiatives such as its Clubcard scheme, said it was a "good start in a competitive environment."
